The putipù is a friction membranophone used in the traditional folk music of southern Italy, especially in Naples and the surrounding area, with the Hornbostel-Sachs classification number 23. It is built as a cylindrical resonator with a membrane stretched over the top, through the centre of which a bamboo rod is fixed; the player rubs the rod with a wet hand, a cloth or a sponge, making the membrane vibrate and sound. It has many variants, with names including caccavella, puti-puti, pignato, cute-cute, cupellone, bufù and cupa-cupa, some of the names imitating the sound.
普蒂普鼓源於義大利南部，特別是那不勒斯地區的民間文化傳統。作為一種摩擦鼓，它的出: The putipù comes from southern Italy, in particular from the folk culture of the Naples area. As a friction drum, its appearance is closely tied to the old instrument-making craft of the Mediterranean. It matured in Naples and the surrounding countryside and gradually became an important part of local folk music performance.
普蒂普鼓的演奏方式獨特，演奏者以濕潤的手、布或海綿摩擦中心的竹製桿，使拉緊的膜產: The putipù is played in a distinctive way: the player rubs the bamboo rod at the centre with a wet hand, a cloth or a sponge, making the tightened membrane resonate and produce its particular timbre. Over several centuries the instrument has given rise to many variants, differing in material and size.
普蒂普鼓音色獨特而原始，具有低沉、粗礪的質感，帶著濃厚的民間樂器特色。其音域主要: The putipù has a distinctive, raw timbre with a low, rough texture, strongly marked by its folk origin. Its range lies mainly in the low and middle frequencies, dark in sound and able to carry. When the player rubs the bamboo rod with a wet finger or cloth, a continuous friction noise intertwines with the resonance of the membrane, making a sound somewhere between a hiss and a low moan. Its way of resonating is quite different from a conventional drumhead instrument and closer to the friction of a string instrument. Compared with modern percussion it is more intimate and raw, like the low call of an animal, and it gives southern Italian folk music a deep, mysterious atmosphere.

隨著時間推移，普蒂普鼓逐漸成為南義大利民間音樂文化的代表樂器。儘管其知名度不如其: In time the putipù became a representative instrument of southern Italian folk music. Although it is less widely known than other European instruments, it still holds an important place in the local folk tradition, standing for the rich musical heritage of southern Italy.

鼓身依變體而異：caccavella 與 pan-bomba 用高品質黏土製成的: The body varies with the variant: the caccavella and the pan-bomba use terracotta of good-quality clay, the putipù itself a small wooden tub or a wooden bowl, the cupellone a larger one, and a large tin such as a tomato tin can serve as well; the rim may be decorated with coloured ribbon. The membrane is mostly animal skin, commonly goat, sheep or rabbit, more rarely donkey or calf, and thick cloth can be used too. The friction rod is bamboo, its lower end passed through the centre of the membrane and tied fast, its upper end often decorated. The instrument is a friction drum, traditionally used in southern Italian folk music.
